qs.q: A new USB device is plugged in, and the OS needs a uniform interface to talk to it without dealing with its hardware details. Which component provides this interface?

c.x: Device controller
Device driver
System bus
Bootstrap program

qs.e: The operating system provides a device driver that understands the device controller and gives the rest of the OS a uniform interface to the device. Device driver

qs.q: Which statement correctly compares the device controller and the device driver?

c.x: The driver moves data between the device and its local buffer; the controller is OS software
The controller is OS software for a uniform interface; the driver is hardware with registers
The controller moves data between the device and its local buffer; the driver is OS software
Both are hardware units, and only the controller is connected to the common bus

qs.e: The device controller is hardware with a local buffer and a set of registers, and it moves data between its peripheral device and that buffer. The device driver is operating-system software that understands the controller and provides a uniform interface. <mark>Controller = hardware, driver = OS software</mark>

qs.q: Which sequence correctly lists the steps of an I/O operation?

c.x: Driver loads controller registers → controller decides the action → controller transfers data to its buffer → controller raises an interrupt → driver returns control to the OS
Controller decides the action → driver loads controller registers → controller transfers data to its buffer → controller raises an interrupt → driver returns control to the OS
Driver loads controller registers → controller decides the action → controller raises an interrupt → controller transfers data to its buffer → driver returns control to the OS
Driver loads controller registers → controller transfers data to its buffer → controller decides the action → controller raises an interrupt → driver returns control to the OS

e: The device driver loads the registers within the device controller.
The device controller determines the action to take based on those registers.
The device controller transfers data between the device and its local buffer.
The device controller generates an interrupt to inform the device driver.
The device driver returns control to the OS (returning the data for a read, or status information for other operations).
<mark>Load registers → decide action → transfer data → interrupt → return control</mark>

qs.q: A system must move a large block of data between a controller's local buffer and main memory while the CPU keeps running other work, with only <u>one</u> interrupt for the whole block. Which mechanism is being used?

c.x: Interrupt-driven I/O
Cache coherency
Timer-based scheduling
Direct memory access

qs.e: In DMA the device controller transfers an entire block directly between its local buffer and main memory with no CPU intervention, generates one interrupt per block, and leaves the CPU free for other work. Direct memory access

qs.q: How does DMA differ from the ordinary I/O operation when moving bulk data?

c.x: DMA generates one interrupt per byte, while ordinary I/O generates one interrupt per block
DMA generates one interrupt per block, while ordinary I/O generates one per byte moved
DMA needs the CPU to copy every byte, while ordinary I/O bypasses the CPU entirely
DMA suits only small transfers, while ordinary I/O is designed for bulk data movement

qs.e: Ordinary interrupt-driven I/O is fine for small amounts of data but gives high CPU overhead for bulk movement. With DMA the controller moves a whole block directly to memory and raises one interrupt per block rather than one per byte. <mark>DMA: one interrupt per block, CPU stays free</mark>

qs.q: A computer has one general-purpose CPU, plus a disk controller, a keyboard controller, and a graphics processor that each execute only a limited instruction set. How is it classified?

c.x: Symmetric multiprocessor system
Asymmetric multiprocessor system
Single-processor system
Clustered system

qs.e: A single-processor system has only one general-purpose processor. Special-purpose processors (disk, keyboard and graphics controllers) support a limited instruction set, cannot execute user processes, and do <u>not</u> turn the system into a multiprocessor. <mark>Single-processor system</mark>

qs.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of a multiprocessor system?

c.x: Its processors are loosely coupled nodes that communicate only over a LAN
It is also known as a parallel system or a tightly-coupled system
It has two or more general-purpose processors in close communication
Its processors share the bus, clock, memory, and peripheral devices

qs.e: A multiprocessor system is a parallel, tightly-coupled system whose processors share the bus, clock, memory and peripherals. Loosely-coupled nodes linked via a LAN describe a clustered system. Loosely coupled nodes over a LAN = clustered, not multiprocessor

qs.q: Which of the following is <u>not</u> an advantage of multiprocessor systems?

c.x: More work is done in less time
Peripherals and power supplies are shared, which lowers the cost
A failed processor only slows the system down instead of halting it
The speed-up ratio with $N$ processors is always exactly $N$

qs.e: The advantages are increased throughput, economy of scale, and increased reliability. The speed-up ratio with $N$ processors is <u>less than</u> $N$, not equal to it. <mark>The speed-up with N processors is less than N</mark>

qs.q: A server's CPU fails, but the system keeps providing service at a lower level that is proportional to the surviving hardware. Which term describes this ability?

c.x: Cache coherency
Graceful degradation
Parallelization
Hot-standby mode

qs.e: Graceful degradation is the ability to continue providing service proportional to the level of surviving hardware. Graceful degradation

qs.q: Which statement correctly compares asymmetric and symmetric multiprocessing?

c.x: Asymmetric treats all processors as peers; symmetric has a boss that schedules the workers
Both have a boss processor, but only symmetric lets the workers perform any task
Asymmetric has a boss that schedules and allocates work; symmetric has peers that perform any task
Symmetric gives workers predefined tasks and is used by few systems; asymmetric is used by most

qs.e: In asymmetric multiprocessing there is a boss-worker relationship: the boss schedules and allocates work, and the workers follow its instructions or have predefined tasks. In symmetric multiprocessing (SMP), used by most systems, all processors are peers and each can perform any task. <mark>Asymmetric = boss-worker; SMP = peers</mark>

qs.q: A single chip contains two CPU cores, each with its own registers and L1 cache, and both cores share an L2 cache that connects to main memory. What kind of system is this?

c.x: A multicore system, which is also a multiprocessor system
A clustered system with two nodes sharing storage
An asymmetric clustering system in hot-standby mode
A single-processor system with special-purpose processors

qs.e: Multiple computing cores on a single chip form a multicore system (here a dual-core design with private registers and L1 caches and a shared L2 cache). Multicore systems are multiprocessor systems. Multicore (dual-core) system

qs.q: Which statement correctly relates multicore and multiprocessor systems?

c.x: Every multiprocessor system is multicore, but not every multicore system is multiprocessor
Multicore and multiprocessor systems are unrelated designs with no overlap
Multicore chips use more power than several single-core chips because of on-chip links
Every multicore system is multiprocessor, but not every multiprocessor system is multicore

qs.e: Multicore systems are multiprocessor systems, but a multiprocessor system may use several separate single-core chips, so <u>not all</u> multiprocessor systems are multicore. On-chip communication is also faster, and one multicore chip uses less power than several single-core chips. <mark>Multicore is a kind of multiprocessor</mark>

qs.q: Which statement correctly compares a multiprocessor system with a clustered system?

c.x: Multiprocessor systems are loosely coupled and share storage via a LAN; clustered systems are tightly coupled
Multiprocessor systems are tightly coupled and share memory; clustered systems are loosely coupled and share storage
Both are tightly coupled, but only clustered systems share a clock and main memory
Both are loosely coupled, but only multiprocessor systems have two or more nodes

qs.e: A multiprocessor system is tightly coupled: its processors share the bus, clock, memory and peripherals. A clustered system is loosely coupled: separate nodes share storage and are linked via a LAN. <mark>Tightly coupled vs loosely coupled</mark>

qs.q: A company runs its service on one active server, while a second node only monitors it and takes over if it fails. Which type of clustering is this?

c.x: Symmetric clustering
Asymmetric multiprocessing
Asymmetric clustering
Symmetric multiprocessing

qs.e: In asymmetric clustering one node is in hot-standby mode monitoring the active server and becomes the active server if it fails, which supports high availability. Asymmetric clustering

qs.q: Which statement correctly compares asymmetric and symmetric clustering?

c.x: Asymmetric keeps one node on hot standby; symmetric has all nodes running applications and monitoring each other
Asymmetric has all nodes running applications and monitoring each other; symmetric keeps one node on hot standby
Asymmetric requires shared memory between the nodes; symmetric needs no shared storage at all
Asymmetric is used for parallelizing applications; symmetric is used only for hot standby

qs.e: In asymmetric clustering one node waits in hot-standby mode and monitors the active server (high availability). In symmetric clustering two or more nodes run applications and monitor each other, which supports high-performance computing better than multiprocessor systems through parallelization. <mark>Standby node vs all nodes working</mark>

qs.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of clustered systems?

c.x: They are composed of two or more individual systems (nodes)
Each node may be a single-processor or a multicore system
The nodes share storage and are closely linked via a LAN
The nodes share one bus, one clock, and one main memory

qs.e: Clustered systems are loosely-coupled sets of nodes that share storage and are linked via a LAN. Sharing one bus, one clock and one memory is a feature of multiprocessor systems. Shared bus, clock and memory = multiprocessor

qs.q: The mode bit of the CPU is currently 1. Which statement is correct?

c.x: The CPU is in kernel mode, so privileged instructions cannot execute
The CPU is in user mode, so privileged instructions cannot execute
The CPU is in user mode, so privileged instructions can execute
The CPU is in kernel mode, so privileged instructions can execute

qs.e: The mode bit indicates kernel (0) or user (1). A value of 1 means user mode, and privileged instructions can execute only in kernel mode (by the OS). Mode bit 1 = user mode, so no privileged instructions

qs.q: Which sequence correctly shows what happens when a user process makes a system call, including the mode bit?

c.x: Process calls system call → trap, mode bit = 1 → system call executes in kernel mode → return, mode bit = 0 → process continues
Process calls system call → system call executes in kernel mode → trap, mode bit = 0 → return, mode bit = 1 → process continues
Process calls system call → trap, mode bit = 0 → system call executes in kernel mode → return, mode bit = 1 → process continues
Process calls system call → trap, mode bit = 0 → return, mode bit = 1 → system call executes in kernel mode → process continues

e: A user process executing in user mode (mode bit = 1) calls a system call.
The call traps to the kernel and the mode bit becomes 0 (kernel mode).
The system call executes in kernel mode.
On return, the mode bit goes back to 1 (user mode).
The user process continues after the return from the system call.
<mark>Call → trap (mode bit 0) → execute in kernel → return (mode bit 1)</mark>

qs.q: Which of the following statements about dual-mode operation is <u>not</u> correct?

c.x: A mode bit of 0 indicates user mode, and a mode bit of 1 indicates kernel mode
Kernel mode is also called supervisor mode, system mode, or privileged mode
Instructions that may cause harm are designated as privileged instructions
User-defined code must execute in user mode to protect the OS from errant users

qs.e: The mode bit is 0 for kernel mode and 1 for user mode, so the first statement reverses them. Kernel = 0, user = 1

qs.q: A CPU supports virtualization and needs a mode with more privileges than user mode but fewer than kernel mode, so that the software that creates and manages virtual machines can run. Which mode is this?

c.x: Supervisor mode
System mode
Guest mode
VMM mode

qs.e: The concept of modes can be extended: a CPU that supports virtualization can have a third mode for the VMM (virtual machine manager), with more privileges than user mode but fewer than kernel mode. Supervisor and system mode are other names for kernel mode. VMM mode

qs.q: Which sequence correctly describes how the OS uses a timer to stop a user program from running too long?

c.x: Control goes to the user program → OS sets the counter → each tick decrements it → counter reaches 0 and an interrupt occurs → control returns to the OS
OS sets the counter → control goes to the user program → each tick decrements it → counter reaches 0 and an interrupt occurs → control returns to the OS
OS sets the counter → control goes to the user program → counter reaches 0 and an interrupt occurs → each tick decrements it → control returns to the OS
OS sets the counter → control goes to the user program → each tick increments it → counter reaches 0 and an interrupt occurs → control returns to the OS

e: The OS sets the counter before turning control over to the user program.
Control goes to the user program.
Every time the clock ticks, the counter is decremented.
When the counter reaches 0, an interrupt occurs.
Control returns to the OS, which may treat the interrupt as a fatal error or give the program more time.
<mark>Set counter → run program → decrement on ticks → interrupt at 0 → back to OS</mark>

qs.q: A user program tries to reload the timer counter with a very large value so that it can keep the CPU forever. How does the OS prevent this?

c.x: By making the clock rate fixed, so the counter can never be changed
By decrementing the counter only when the program makes a system call
By making instructions that modify the timer privileged, so only the OS can run them
By terminating every program as soon as the counter is set

qs.e: The timer lets the OS regain control from a program that runs too long, so instructions that modify the content of the timer are privileged and can execute only in kernel mode. Timer-modifying instructions are privileged

qs.q: Which statement correctly compares batch and multiprogramming systems when the running job waits for an I/O operation?

c.x: Batch leaves the CPU idle until the job continues; multiprogramming lets the OS pick another job in memory
Batch picks another job from memory; multiprogramming leaves the CPU idle until the job continues
Both leave the CPU idle, but only multiprogramming offers direct interaction with the user
Both pick another job, but only batch keeps several jobs in main memory at once

qs.e: In a batch system the CPU remains idle while the running job waits for I/O (low CPU utilization). In a multiprogramming system several jobs are kept in main memory, so the OS picks another job to start or continue, and the CPU is always executing a job. <mark>Batch: CPU idles; multiprogramming: another job runs</mark>

qs.q: Many users work with their own programs at the same time, and the CPU switches between jobs so frequently that each user can interact with a running program. Which type of system is this?

c.x: Batch system
Multiprogramming system
Real-time embedded system
Time-sharing system

qs.e: A time-sharing (multitasking) system is an interactive extension of multiprogramming: the CPU switches between jobs so frequently that the user can interact with each program while it runs. Multiprogramming alone still has no direct interaction. Time-sharing system

qs.q: Which of the following is not a feature the OS must provide to support a multiprogramming system?

c.x: I/O routines performed only by the OS
Direct interaction between user and job
Memory management for several jobs
CPU scheduling to select a job

qs.e: Multiprogramming needs I/O routines, CPU scheduling, memory management and resource allocation. It increases CPU utilization, but there is <u>still no</u> direct interaction between the user and the system. <mark>No direct interaction in multiprogramming</mark>

qs.q: Which statement correctly compares client-server and peer-to-peer computing?

c.x: In P2P a server is a bottleneck, while in client-server several nodes can provide the service
In client-server every node must first join the system, while P2P nodes need no joining
In client-server a server can be a bottleneck, while in P2P several nodes can provide the service
In client-server each node acts as both server and client, while P2P has fixed servers

qs.e: In client-server systems the server satisfies the clients' requests and can become a bottleneck. In P2P systems all nodes are peers (each may act as a server or a client), so several nodes can provide the service. <mark>Server bottleneck vs several service providers</mark>

qs.q: A company keeps sensitive workloads on a cloud used only by the company, and runs other workloads on a cloud that is available to anyone via the Internet. Which cloud model does it use?

c.x: Hybrid cloud
Private cloud
Public cloud
Federated cloud

qs.e: A hybrid cloud includes both private cloud components (used only by the company that owns it) and public cloud components (available to anyone via the Internet). Hybrid cloud

qs.q: One physical computer runs three guest virtual machines, each with its own OS. Which component runs the guests, manages their resource use, and protects each guest from the others?

c.x: Device driver
Load balancer
Bootstrap program
Virtual machine manager

qs.e: The virtual machine manager runs the guest machines, manages their resource use, and protects each guest from the others, while the host and the guests share the hardware. Virtual machine manager

qs.q: Which option correctly matches the cloud service models with what they provide?

c.x: SaaS: servers or storage; PaaS: applications; IaaS: a software stack
SaaS: applications; PaaS: a software stack; IaaS: servers or storage
SaaS: a software stack; PaaS: servers or storage; IaaS: applications
SaaS: applications; PaaS: servers or storage; IaaS: a software stack

qs.e: Software as a service provides applications (e.g. Google Docs), platform as a service provides a software stack (e.g. Google Firebase), and infrastructure as a service provides servers or storage over the Internet. SaaS = applications, PaaS = software stack, IaaS = servers or storage

qs.q: A medical imaging system must finish its processing within well-defined, fixed time limits, or the system fails. Which kind of system is this?

c.x: Time-sharing system
Batch system
Real-time embedded system
Desktop system

qs.e: A real-time system has well-defined, fixed time constraints, and processing must be done within them or the system fails. Embedded systems almost always run real-time operating systems. Real-time embedded system
